# coderforge_container_service (Data Source)

Look up a container service by id or by name, whether or not Terraform manages it. Its `node_state` gives the addresses of the machines behind it, which is what a port forwarding rule needs.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# By name...
data "coderforge_container_service" "edge" {
  name = "edge-proxy"
}

# ...or by the platform's id, which is unambiguous.
data "coderforge_container_service" "api" {
  id = "0002"
}

# Forward a host port to the first node of the service.
resource "coderforge_network_rule" "edge_http" {
  src_port  = "80"
  dest_ip   = data.coderforge_container_service.edge.node_state[0].ip
  dest_port = "80"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `id` (String) Four-digit service id. Specify this or `name`.
- `name` (String) Service name. Specify this or `id`.

### Read-Only

- `containers` (List of String) Service names declared by the compose file.
- `created_at` (String)
- `desired_state` (String)
- `env_param_rid` (String)
- `env_secret_rid` (String)
- `managed_by` (String)
- `message` (String)
- `network_rid` (String)
- `node_state` (Attributes List) The machines backing this service. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--node_state))
- `nodes` (Number)
- `provisioner_name` (String) Provisioner script run on each node.
- `raw_status` (String)
- `rid` (String)
- `state` (String) Normalised state.
- `updated_at` (String)
- `version` (Number)

<a id="nestedatt--node_state"></a>
### Nested Schema for `node_state`

Read-Only:

- `index` (Number)
- `ip` (String)
- `message` (String)
- `status` (String)
- `vm_name` (String)
